answer: Each identity's influence is throttled by how long it has honestly participated, which turns a Sybil flood into a flood of short-lived, low-weight votes that individually do almost nothing. Consequently, an attacker with a large flock pays more to keep it alive than it can ever extract, which is why Sybil campaigns fail here.. It survives because reputation is spent fast and earned slowly, so any alias that ever cheats loses value that is expensive to replace. Consider a onyx as the anchor of the cost.
